idea-plugin.name: Sightline
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Code inside Android Studio, with reviewable changes and controlled tool execution.

Sightline provides a native Android Studio interface for a locally installed Claude Code CLI.

Use it to:

  • Chat with Claude without leaving Android Studio.
  • Attach files and IDE context, and remove any of it before you send.
  • Review tool requests and proposed changes as diffs before they apply.
  • Stop a turn without losing the conversation, and pick up where you left off.
  • Watch what a subagent is doing inside the task that started it.
  • Run your own Claude Code commands, skills and plugins from the panel.
  • Inspect structured build, test and diagnostic results.

Android-aware. Sightline knows your build variant, connected device, module and running process, so you don't have to explain them. It reads Gradle failures into typed diagnoses, resolves crashes back to the line that threw, picks the tests worth running for what you changed, and audits your merged manifest. Logcat is redacted before it can reach a prompt.

Requires the Claude Code CLI (the claude command), installed and authenticated separately. Sightline does not provide Claude access, does not handle your credentials, and has no login screen or backend of its own.

No telemetry. No analytics, no usage statistics, nothing sent anywhere except to the local claude process you started. Sightline itself writes no transcript; note that the Claude Code CLI keeps its own session history under ~/.claude/projects/, under your account and its own retention rules, which is what lets a conversation resume.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.11.0 — a calmer, easier-to-follow conversation.

Each reply reads as a sequence of steps. Every step Claude takes sits on a thin line down the left with a dot beside it: green when a tool finished, red when it failed, a hollow ring when you denied it, and teal while it is running or waiting for you. Tool steps lead with the tool's name — Bash, Read, Edit — and a file appears as its name, which you can click to open.

Commands show what ran and what came back. You see the command and the first few lines of its output; longer output fades out, says how many lines are hidden, and opens with a click. Thinking takes one line — “Thought for 4s”.

You can always tell where things stand. A running reply ends with a line saying it is still working, with the elapsed time — or that it is waiting for you. Scroll through a long answer and the question that asked for it stays pinned at the top.

A tidier message box, with its own model button. Steps are now shown by default; for the one-line summary instead, choose More ▸ Hide technical details.

Fixed: warning and note callouts showed as plain text on Android Studio 2026.2.
